_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 6 $826D-$8434: the move with wall sliding and the blocking table. The generators subtract these.

regions.name: Move: the new position
regions.description: MOVE WITH WALLS (slot `$8009`; X = the object, normally the player in the labyrinth): `$16` := y fraction `$0758` + y speed fraction `$05C0`; `$17` := y `$0518` + y speed `$05D8` + carry + the foot offset `$06B0` (8): the probe y, i.e. where the ship's feet would be; `$18` := x fraction `$0770` + `$05F0`; `$19` := x `$0530` + x speed `$0608` + carry. Nothing is stored yet. RUN: 1,500 random states (random class maps, positions and velocities) on the model equalled an independent model of this reading in every output.

regions.name: Move: same cell row?
regions.description: `$6F` := 0. The row of the new probe y (`$17 AND $F0`) against the row of the old one (`$0518 + $06B0`, same mask): equal sets `$6F` bit 7 (the move stays inside one cell row).

regions.name: Move: same cell column? Then nothing to check
regions.description: The column of the new x against the old one: equal sets `$6F` bit 6. Both set (`$6F` = `$C0`): the ship stays in its cell, `$6C` := 0 and the move is accepted at `$840C`.

regions.name: Move: the class of the target cell (`$6C`)
regions.description: The class map `$0400-$045F` is 8 bytes a cell row, two cells a byte: index = (probe y AND `$F0`) / 2 + new column / 2, the high nibble for an even column and the low for an odd one. An index of `$60` or more (below the 12 rows of the room) reads as class 9. `$6C` := the class of (new row, new column): the diagonal cell. (The same lookup is repeated three times in this routine.)

regions.name: Move: column unchanged
regions.description: `$6F` bit 6 set (the ship stayed in its column) copies `$6C` to `$6D` (`JMP $8317`); the cell straight above or below is the diagonal cell.

regions.name: Move: the class of the y-step cell (`$6D`)
regions.description: (new row, OLD column): the cell reached by moving in y only. The old x is shifted down five bits to the byte index (the last bit shifted out is the column's low bit).

regions.name: Move: row unchanged
regions.description: `$6D` stored. `$6F` bit 7 set (same row) copies `$6C` to `$6E` (`JMP $8345`).

regions.name: Move: the class of the x-step cell (`$6E`)
regions.description: (OLD row, new column): the cell reached by moving in x only.

regions.name: Move: which of them block
regions.description: `$6E` stored. `$10` := `$8425[$6C]`, `$11` := `$8425[$6D]`: 1 where the class blocks the ship (classes 4-10 and 14; the table is below).

regions.name: Move: `$12` - the x-step cell is NOT consulted
regions.description: The code does `LDA $6E` and then `LDA $8425,Y` with Y still holding `$6D`: there is no `TAY`, so the loaded `$6E` is thrown away and `$12` := `$8425[$6D]`, a copy of `$11`. It looks like a missed instruction. **Effect, measured:** a model that reads `$8425[$6E]` here disagreed with the real routine in 9 of 1,500 random states; the model that copies `$11` agreed in all of them. So a move where only the x-step cell blocks is judged as if it were free in x.

regions.name: Move: free? accept
regions.description: `$10 OR $11 OR $12` all zero: no cell in the way, accept the whole move at `$840C`.

regions.name: Move: blocked - snap y to the cell edge
regions.description: Y speed non-negative (bit 7 clear, which includes 0): y := ((y + foot) OR `$0F`) - foot, the bottom edge of the cell; negative: ((y + foot) AND `$F0`) - foot, the top edge. Stored in `$0518` at once.

regions.name: Move: blocked - snap x to the cell edge
regions.description: X speed non-negative: x OR `$0F`, else x AND `$F0`, stored in `$0530`.

regions.name: Move: blocked, same column (vertical move)
regions.description: `$6F` bit 6: the diagonal cell `$10` blocked leaves y snapped and takes only the new x (`$8415`); free accepts all (`$840C`).

regions.name: Move: blocked, same row (horizontal move)
regions.description: `$6F` bit 7: `$10` clear accepts all; blocked takes the new y (it stays in the row) and keeps x snapped.

regions.name: Move: blocked, a diagonal crossing: which axis moved further
regions.description: Both row and column changed. `$13` := |probe y - snapped y - foot| and A := |new x - snapped x| (measured from the already snapped position), compared.

regions.name: Move: a diagonal crossing, equal distances
regions.description: `$11` set: x only if `$12` is clear, else neither. `$11` clear: y only if `$12` is set, else neither.

regions.name: Move: a diagonal crossing, y moved further
regions.description: `$11` set: x only if `$12` clear, else neither. `$11` clear: y only if the diagonal `$10` blocks, else everything.

regions.name: Move: a diagonal crossing, x moved further
regions.description: `$12` set: y only if `$11` clear, else neither. `$12` clear: x only if `$10` blocks, else everything.

regions.name: Move: commit y
regions.description: `$0518` := `$17` - foot (the new y). 'Everything' and 'y only' arrive here or at `$83AD`.

regions.name: Move: commit the fractions
regions.description: `$0758` := `$16` and `$0770` := `$18` in every case, including a blocked move: only the whole-pixel position is held back, the sub-pixel parts always advance. RTS. Outputs for the callers: `$6C` diagonal class, `$6D` y-step class, `$6E` x-step class, `$6F` bit 7 same row, bit 6 same column.

regions.name: Blocking by cell class: 16 x 0/1
regions.description: `00 00 00 00 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 00 00 00 01 00`: classes 4-10 and 14 stop the ship (the breakable and solid blocks and the key-door cover, per the cell-class notes); 0-3, 11-13 and 15 do not.
